text_blocks.snippet: Car loan interest rates in India currently range from approximately 7.70% to 14.75% per annum, depending on the bank, loan type, and the borrower's credit profile. Several banks offer competitive rates, with some offering lower rates for electric vehicles to promote eco-friendly transportation.

list.snippet: Bank: Different banks offer varying interest rates, with public sector banks sometimes offering slightly lower rates than private sector banks.
Loan Type: Interest rates can differ for new car loans, used car loans, and electric vehicle loans.
Credit Score: A strong credit score typically results in a lower interest rate.
Relationship with the Bank: Existing customers of a bank may be offered better interest rates.
Loan Tenure: Longer loan tenures may result in higher overall interest costs, even if the monthly installments are lower.
Car Segment: The type and cost of the car can also impact the interest rate.

text_blocks.snippet: Example Interest Rates from Different Banks:

list.snippet: Union Bank of India: Offers rates starting from 7.70% onwards for new car loans.
Axis Bank: Offers rates from 8.90% onwards for new cars.
Bank of Baroda: Offers rates from 8.75% for fixed and 8.40% for floating rates on new cars.
State Bank of India (SBI): Offers rates starting from 8.65% for new cars and 8.60% for electric vehicles.
ICICI Bank: Offers rates starting from 9.1% for new cars.
IDFC FIRST Bank: Offers rates starting from 9.99% for new cars.
HDFC Bank: Offers rates from 8.44% to 20.99% for new cars.
Bank of Maharashtra: Offers rates from 7.70% to 12.00%.

text_blocks.snippet: Tips for Getting a Lower Interest Rate:

list.title: Improve your credit score:
list.snippet: A higher credit score will make you a more attractive borrower.

list.title: Compare offers from multiple banks:
list.snippet: Don't settle for the first offer you receive. Shop around and compare rates from different lenders.

list.title: Negotiate with the bank:
list.snippet: If you have a good credit score and a strong relationship with a bank, you may be able to negotiate a lower interest rate.

list.title: Consider a shorter loan tenure:
list.snippet: A shorter loan tenure will result in higher monthly installments but lower overall interest costs.

text_blocks.snippet: By considering these factors and taking the time to compare offers, you can find the best car loan interest rate for your needs.
